summary: This document defines a new Mobile IPv4 extension that lets a Foreign Agent report status information to a mobile node. Previously, a foreign agent adding such information could break the mobile node's ability to verify the home agent's authentication data. The new extension gives the status information its own place in the message. It updates RFC 3344.

eli5.summary: Imagine a friend passing your letter along and scribbling a note on it, which ruins the seal. This gives the friend a separate card for notes, so the seal stays unbroken.

subtitle: A separate slot in Mobile IPv4 replies where a foreign agent can report errors without breaking the home agent's authentication.

tldr.problem: A foreign agent sometimes has to put status information into a Mobile IPv4 Registration Reply. Doing so used to destroy the mobile node's ability to verify the authentication data supplied by the home agent.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a new non-skippable extension, the FA Error Extension, appended to the Registration Reply. It carries the foreign agent's status code and leaves the home agent's data untouched.
tldr.outcome: The mobile node can still verify that the reply came from its home agent. The RFC updates RFC 3344 so that a foreign agent reports status 68 through this extension instead of rewriting the reply.

today: RFC 4636 is a Proposed Standard and is not marked as obsoleted or updated by any other RFC. It updates RFC 3344 for the case where the home agent fails authentication.

sections.title: The Problem With Foreign Agent Status
sections.content:
In Mobile IPv4 (RFC 3344), a mobile node registers through a foreign agent and the reply comes back from its home agent. The home agent authenticates its reply, so the mobile node can check that it really came from the home agent.

The trouble, as the abstract puts it, is that a foreign agent cannot supply status information without destroying the mobile node's ability to verify that authentication data. RFC 4636 fixes this by giving the foreign agent a better place to put its status: a new extension that does not disturb what the home agent supplied.
sections.eli5: A helper in the middle sometimes needs to say something about your message. Before, the only way was to change the message itself, which spoiled the proof of who wrote it.

sections.title: The FA Error Extension Format
sections.content:
The FA Error Extension follows the Short Extension format of Mobile IPv4 and is not skippable. It has four one-byte fields: Type (45), Length (2), Sub-Type (0) and Status.

The Status field carries a status code that the foreign agent uses to give status information to the mobile node.
sections.eli5: It is a tiny four-part note: what kind of note it is, how long it is, a sub-label, and the actual code saying what went wrong.

sections.title: Where and How It Is Used
sections.content:
The extension is valid only inside Mobile IPv4 Registration Reply messages. Because it is not skippable, a mobile node that cannot correctly interpret it MUST NOT use the care-of address from the reply until it has sent another Registration Request and received a successful Registration Reply.

Allowed status codes are in the range 64-127. The RFC lists the currently specified ones, as defined in RFC 3344 for foreign agent use. Codes for this extension must not be defined differently for the Code field of Registration Reply messages.

When a foreign agent appends the extension to a reply received from the home agent, it has to update the UDP Length field in the UDP header to account for the extra 4 bytes.

This RFC updates RFC 3344. When the home agent fails authentication, the foreign agent used to change the reply's status field to 68. Now it should append the FA Error Extension containing status value 68.
sections.eli5: The note can only ride along on a reply. If you cannot read the note, you must not trust the new address until you ask again and get a good answer.

sections.title: Mobile Node and Foreign Agent Behavior
sections.content:
If a mobile node receives a successful Registration Reply (status code 0 or 1) with an FA Error Extension saying the foreign agent is not honoring that reply, the mobile node SHOULD send a deregistration message to the home agent. That keeps the home agent from holding a registration that disagrees with the foreign agent's.

When a foreign agent denies a successful Registration Reply, it SHOULD send a Registration Revocation message (RFC 3543) to the home agent, if a mobility security association exists between them.
sections.eli5: If the helper says it will not pass your message on, you tell your home base to forget it. The helper can also tell home base itself, if they trust each other.

sections.title: Number Allocations
sections.content:
The RFC reserves one number for the extension from the space of non-skippable mobility extensions (0-127) defined for Mobile IPv4. It also creates a new number space of sub-types for this extension type, with sub-type zero allocated to this extension. Future allocations from it require expert review.

The status codes allowed in the extension are a subset of those in RFC 3344. If new Mobile IPv4 status codes are defined later, each definition must say whether the code may be used in the FA Error Extension.
sections.eli5: The RFC asks for one official number for its note type and starts a fresh list of sub-labels, where it takes the first spot.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension improves Mobile IPv4 security because the mobile node can be sure of the authenticity of the home agent's data while still receiving the foreign agent's status.

The extension itself is unauthenticated, though. Often the mobile node has no security association with the foreign agent, so it cannot tell that the foreign agent sending the extended reply is the one that received its request. A malicious foreign agent could make the mobile node act as if registration had failed even though the home agent and a correct foreign agent accepted it. To reduce that risk, the mobile node MAY delay processing such denied replies for a short while to see whether a successful reply arrives from the foreign agent.
sections.eli5: Anyone in the middle could write a fake 'it failed' note. So the mobile node may wait a moment in case a real success message shows up.
